newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH STRIKE HARD AGAINST GROWING HOOLIGAN MENACE.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH STRIKE HARD AGAINST GROWING HOOLIGAN MENACE.

text.p: The Dutch government announced on Wednesday it was cracking down on football hooliganism, with offenders liable to summary arrest and the possible introduction of identity cards for fans.

"(We will) identify as many people as possible, arrest (them) on the spot, arrest after the match and arrest on the basis of video pictures and other material," said Justice Minister Winnie Sorgdrager.

Her comments to journalists came after a meeting of several ministers called following the first ever death from football violence 10 days ago, and general agreement that soccer hooliganism was on the increase.

The ministers plan to present a list of measures to parliament next week. A steering group which they plan to set up may consider strengthening the powers of local police chiefs, and introducing identity cards for fans, officials said.

"The key to changing the sports world is to draw the supporters out of their anonymity...We are looking at...whether club cards can be upgraded into some form of personal card," said junior sports minister Erica Terpstra.
The football-related death came as rival gangs from Ajax Amsterdam and Feyenoord Rotterdam clashed 10 days ago, on a day when the two teams were not even playing.
